articles.title: Veterans Day wreath-laying restrictions: Everything to know if you're attending the Memorial at Arlington National Cemetery
articles.standfirst: Visitors can still attend the national Veterans Day observance on November 11, but a major change means the public will no longer be able to watch the traditional wreath-laying ceremony at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier
articles.summary: Visitors can still attend the national Veterans Day observance on November 11, but a major change means the public will no longer be able to watch the traditional wreath-laying ceremony at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier
articles.body:
Americans planning to mark Veterans Day at Arlington National Cemetery in Virginia will need to pay attention to new restrictions affecting one of the day's most significant traditions.

The cemetery has confirmed that public access to the annual wreath-laying ceremony at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier will be restricted to official participants on Wednesday, November 11, 2026.

This represents a departure from previous years, when members of the public could gather to witness the solemn tribute.

However, the restriction does not mean Arlington is closing its doors to everyone wishing to attend the national commemoration.

The 73rd annual National Veterans Day Observance will remain free and open to the public, with the main program scheduled to take place inside the Memorial Amphitheater at 11 a.m.

The announcement is particularly important for visitors who may have assumed that attending the public event would also give them access to the wreath-laying itself.

Those are now two separate parts of the program, and only authorized participants will be permitted to attend the ceremony at the Tomb.

The cemetery has not publicly provided a detailed explanation for the change, so visitors should avoid assuming that the restriction applies to every activity taking place on the grounds.

What visitors can expect at the Memorial Amphitheater

Although the public cannot watch the wreath-laying ceremony, there is still a substantial program planned for Veterans Day.

The United States Coast Guard Band and the U.S. Air Force Singing Sergeants are scheduled to perform a musical prelude beginning at 10:30 a.m. The national observance will follow at 11 a.m., featuring a parade of colors by veterans' organizations and remarks from dignitaries.

Seating inside the Memorial Amphitheater will be available on a first-come, first-served basis. There is no admission charge, but visitors should arrive early because capacity is limited.

The cemetery has also introduced specific transportation arrangements for the event. Free parking will be available at the Welcome Center parking lot between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m.

However, visitors attending the observance must use the tram to travel between the Welcome Center and the Memorial Amphitheater.

Walking to and from the amphitheater is strictly prohibited during the event. Tram operations are expected to begin at approximately 8:30 a.m. and continue until capacity is reached. Arlington recommends arriving at the tram no later than 9:45 a.m. to improve the chances of securing access.

Security screening will also be mandatory before entering the cemetery and amphitheater.

Which items are prohibited?

Visitors should be particularly careful about what they bring. Arlington has published a list of restricted items, and security personnel may confiscate prohibited belongings.

Items that cannot be brought into the event include:

- Large bags and backpacks.

- Glass, metal or insulated containers, including hard water bottles and soda cans.

- Alcohol, coolers and picnic baskets.

- Tripods and selfie sticks.

- Weapons, ammunition, explosives and pepper spray.

- Aerosol containers, lighters and laser pointers.

- Air horns and other items considered potential safety hazards.

Clear disposable plastic water bottles are permitted. However, hard water bottles will be confiscated at the security checkpoint and will not be returned.

The cemetery also warns that the restrictions may be updated depending on security requirements. Visitors should therefore check the official announcement before setting off.

Can families still visit gravesites?

Yes. Family pass holders who need to visit the graves of loved ones can still enter through the main entrance on Memorial Avenue.

Nevertheless, they should expect delays when entering and leaving the cemetery. Movement restrictions and temporary freezes inside the grounds may affect visitors during the national observance.

Anyone unable to attend in person can also watch the event through the livestream announced by Arlington National Cemetery.

Why the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier matters

The restrictions are particularly notable because the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier has been central to national remembrance for more than a century.

The monument was dedicated on November 11, 1921, when an unidentified American service member from World War I was laid to rest following a national ceremony attended by President Warren G. Harding and international dignitaries.

It represents American service members whose remains were never identified, ensuring that those who died without their identities being known are still remembered and honored.

The opportunity for the public to lay wreaths at the Tomb has long been an important part of Arlington's commemorative traditions.

For anyone planning to attend this year's Veterans Day observance, the key distinction is simple: the Memorial Amphitheater program remains open to the public, but the wreath-laying ceremony itself is reserved for official participants.

Arriving early, following the transportation arrangements and checking the prohibited-items list will help visitors avoid unnecessary problems on November 11.

articles.title: William James, Philosopher and psychologist: "The great use of life is to spend it for something that will outlast it"
articles.standfirst: The influential American thinker believed that a meaningful existence should be measured by more than personal success
articles.summary: The influential American thinker believed that a meaningful existence should be measured by more than personal success
articles.body:
What makes a life worthwhile? For American philosopher and psychologist William James , the answer was not simply the pursuit of wealth, recognition or individual happiness.

Instead, he emphasized the importance of contributing to something with a value that extends beyond one's own existence.

His famous reflection, "The great use of life is to spend it for something that will outlast it," captures an idea that remains relevant more than a century after his death. It encourages people to consider the consequences of their actions and the kind of legacy they hope to leave behind.

The quotation is commonly associated with James , and research into its origins has traced an earlier version to a letter he wrote to Polish philosopher Wincenty Lutoslawski on November 13, 1900.

In that letter, the wording was recorded as: "The great use of a life," James said, "is to spend it for something that outlasts it." The letter was subsequently documented in the second volume of The Thought and Character of William James , edited by Ralph Barton Perry and published in 1935.

The central message is straightforward: a person's contribution can continue to matter long after their lifetime has ended.

That contribution does not necessarily have to involve a major historical achievement. Supporting others, sharing knowledge, creating something meaningful or working toward a better society can all represent ways of building a lasting legacy.

A thinker who helped shape modern psychology and philosophy

Born in New York City on January 11, 1842, James became one of the most influential intellectual figures in American history. Although he initially studied medicine at Harvard, his interests developed into psychology and philosophy, fields in which he would leave a substantial mark.

His 1890 publication, The Principles of Psychology, became a landmark work. It explored subjects including consciousness, memory, emotion, habit and the relationship between the mind and the body.

James also helped establish psychology as an academic discipline at Harvard, where he taught and influenced generations of students.

He was also a leading figure in American pragmatism, a philosophical approach that considers the practical consequences of ideas.

Rather than treating philosophy as an exercise detached from everyday life, James examined how beliefs and theories relate to human experience.

That outlook helps explain the enduring appeal of his words about spending life on something that will survive its creator. His philosophy placed considerable importance on the relationship between ideas, choices and their effects on the world.

James explored these questions in other influential publications, including The Varieties of Religious Experience (1902) and Pragmatism (1907). His work attracted attention from thinkers across different disciplines and continues to be studied today.

James died on August 26, 1910, aged 68, but his intellectual influence continued through his books, students and the development of modern psychology and philosophy.

Ultimately, his quotation offers a challenge to think beyond immediate rewards. It suggests that a meaningful life is not defined exclusively by what someone accumulates or accomplishes for themselves, but also by what they leave behind for others.

Whether through family, education, creativity, public service or personal relationships, the opportunity to make a lasting difference is available in many forms.

articles.title: Powerball Winning Numbers: Results for Monday, November 9 drawing for the $30 million jackpot
articles.standfirst: The Powerball jackpot has climbed to an estimated $30 million after the previous drawing produced no grand-prize winner
articles.summary: The Powerball jackpot has climbed to an estimated $30 million after the previous drawing produced no grand-prize winner
articles.body:
The latest Powerball drawing is scheduled for Monday night, meaning players will have to wait until after the draw to discover whether anyone has matched all six numbers and claimed the estimated $30 million jackpot.

According to the official Powerball website, the November 9 prize has an estimated annuity value of $30 million, while the cash option stands at approximately $12.9 million before taxes.

The drawing is scheduled for 10:59 p.m. Eastern Time, with winning numbers published after the results have been verified.

The previous drawing took place on Saturday, November 7, when the winning combination was 3, 36, 37, 56 and 61, with 21 as the red Powerball . The Power Play multiplier was 2X.

No ticket matched all six numbers, allowing the jackpot to continue growing for Monday's draw.

Players should check their tickets against the official results once the November 9 numbers become available rather than relying on unofficial predictions or numbers circulating before the drawing.

A new jackpot cycle follows the $847 million New Jersey win

The current prize comes after an extraordinary run that ended with a single ticket winning an $847 million Powerball jackpot in New Jersey.

The winning ticket for the November 4 drawing was purchased at Wegmans Food Market on Farm View in Montvale, Bergen County. Its numbers were 15, 34, 41, 53 and 56, with 21 as the Powerball and a 2X Power Play multiplier.

The prize was the ninth-largest jackpot in Powerball history. The winner can choose between receiving the advertised $847 million through an annuity or taking a one-time cash payment of $363.1 million, with both figures calculated before taxes. The winner had not been publicly identified in the latest reports.

Wegmans is also set to receive a $30,000 retailer bonus for selling the winning ticket. However, the company announced that the money would be donated to the Community FoodBank of New Jersey through its Check Out Hunger campaign, turning the sale into a contribution to local hunger-relief efforts.

How much could Monday's Powerball winner receive?

If a player wins the November 9 jackpot, they will face the familiar choice between an annuity and a lump-sum payment.

The advertised $30 million prize represents the annuity option, distributed through 30 graduated payments over 29 years. Alternatively, the winner can select the estimated $12.9 million cash value, which is paid as a single amount before applicable taxes.

Powerball tickets cost $2 per play, with players selecting five white-ball numbers from 1 to 69 and one red Powerball number from 1 to 26. The odds of matching all six numbers and winning the jackpot are approximately 1 in 292.2 million.

The optional Power Play feature costs an additional $1 and can multiply eligible non-jackpot prizes. It does not increase the advertised jackpot itself.

Monday's drawing is one of three regular weekly Powerball draws, which take place every Monday, Wednesday and Saturday. Ticket sales close at different times depending on the state or jurisdiction, so players should check their local lottery's deadline.

The November 9 winning numbers and Power Play result will be added once the drawing has taken place and the official results are confirmed. Until then, the $30 million jackpot remains up for grabs.
